page: Amazon Web Services r6in.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are supplemented by 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware support for cryptographic acceleration, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions. System memory provides 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive workloads.

Network infrastructure on the instance delivers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps for network-bound and EBS-optimized operations. The server does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring all persistent and non-volatile data to rely on external network-attached volumes. In addition, no hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate reliable mid-tier compute and memory throughput across standardized tests. The instance achieved 1,616.0 points in Geekbench single-core and 9,791.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21,082.67. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 95.46 GB/sec with write throughput at 56.42 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the configuration handled 15.9 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 22.59 GB/sec in static web serving. Small language model text generation was strong at 272.59 tokens per second on a 135M model, though prompt processing degraded to the bottom quartile at 31.94 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, r6in.4xlarge optimizes budget allocation toward expansive RAM capacity and enhanced network throughput rather than raw compute clock density or local disk IOPS. It is directly aligned with memory-bound applications, including in-memory databases such as Redis, caching layers, distributed data processing nodes, and intermediate ETL staging pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive and network-demanding workloads. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, along with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations place it in the average performance tier for standard CPU and memory operations, reaching 15.9 million Redis SET operations per second and 95.46 GB/sec large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, r6in.4xlarge represents a balanced operational configuration for enterprise caching layers, in-memory datastores, and large-scale data transformation services.
